acceptanceCriteria.statement: The host star's temperature is recorded on the body record and reaches the condition vector as a real measured value, not a default.

verifyVia.input: Generate lab-procedural-0..199 headlessly and read the condition vector and _provenance for every planet.
verifyVia.observable: A star-temperature field is present on 100% of generated planets and its _provenance reads 'measured' on 100% of them. Today the comparable figure is 0/167. Report the measured count, never the field's name-resolution count.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Adding the star field to the body record moves Instrument B's RECORD SHAPE assertion, and that move is declared and deliberately re-blessed rather than absorbed.

verifyVia.input: Run tests/body-identity-fence.test.js before and after the generator change.
verifyVia.observable: RECORD SHAPE reds and names the added field. BODY IDENTITY and DRAW STREAM stay green, proving the field is additive and did not move the RNG stream. The re-bless is a separate commit naming the field. A green run here would mean the field was never actually added.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Ground cover colour is chosen by which kind of star the world orbits — the spectrum picks a palette family, and the families are authored rather than derived.

verifyVia.input: Sample the resolved land palette across generated worlds grouped by primary spectral class (M / K / G / A).
verifyVia.observable: The pigment resolved for each class comes from that class's authored family, and the four families are distinguishable from one another. A world's family is a function of its primary only.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: An M-dwarf world does not read green — it comes out dark, oxblood or violet, something that looks like it grew under a red sun.

verifyVia.input: Fly to a generated M-dwarf system with a vegetated world and view it from orbit.
verifyVia.observable: The vegetated ground is visibly not-green and sits inside the authored M-dwarf family.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A Sun-like star still gives green continents — Max's D-9 ruling survives the change.

verifyVia.input: Fly to a generated G-star system with an Earth-like vegetated world and view it from orbit.
verifyVia.observable: Vegetated land reads green. This is the ordinary case and it must not be sacrificed to make the strange cases strange.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The pigment rides through albedoTransfer's opts.extra and is scaled by the same transfer as the ground endmembers.

verifyVia.input: Unit-test the transfer with a pigment supplied for each authored family.
verifyVia.observable: Pigment albedo sits in the intended relation to the rock it replaces. The known failure to fence against: the first port pushed raw BIO_PIGMENT to the shader and the canopy rendered at ~43% of intended albedo, ~4x darker than its rock, instead of the intended ~1.75x.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Sol is untouched by the whole change.

verifyVia.input: Load Sol and compare its bodies against a pre-change capture.
verifyVia.observable: Sol renders identically. Sol runs 18 NASA textures through a different renderer with no world-engine condition fields and is excluded in code; any movement here means the change leaked past that carve-out.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The four palette families are Max's authored colours, judged in the running build while moving between systems — not from a swatch sheet.

verifyVia.input: Max flies between an M-dwarf, K-dwarf, G-star and A-star system in the real build, with the pigment change behind a bare-key A/B he can flip while moving.
verifyVia.observable: Max's judgment that the four families cohere as somewhere he wants to fly to, and that the alien worlds read alien rather than merely miscoloured. Holistic acceptance — no agent drives or passes this.

src/worldengine/base/emission-e.js blackbodyEmission(tempK) — existing Planckian-locus chromaticity law anchored to real blackbody sRGB; reusable for deriving the family boundaries even though the family colours are authored
src/worldengine/base/surfaceMaterial.js BIO_PIGMENT + surfacePaletteOf(condition) — the constant being replaced by a per-world law
outputs: landPalette on the body record, via applyAlbedoTransfer — the orbital ground colour Max actually sees
src/generation/PlanetGenerator.js:809 the applyAlbedoTransfer call carrying pigment through opts.extra
the lab material's palette path, which B3 is concurrently wiring — the collision surface named in intent.md
